note: Lens prompts are original wording for review panels. A lens sets what a reviewer looks for. It does not make a reviewer independent: independence comes from harness and model family, see docs/REVIEW-PANEL.md.

lenses.title: Contract fit
lenses.question: Does the artifact do what the original task contract says, no more and no less?
asks: Which stated requirement or acceptance criterion has no matching change or evidence?
Which change answers a requirement nobody stated?
Does the done criterion in the contract hold when read cold, without the author's explanation?

lenses.title: Regression risk
lenses.question: What existing behavior could this change break, and which check would notice?
asks: Which callers, data shapes or configs depend on the old behavior?
Would the existing tests fail if the change were reverted, or do they pass either way?
What input class was never exercised?

lenses.title: Security and abuse
lenses.question: How could an attacker or a careless user turn this against the system?
asks: Where does untrusted input reach a command, query, path or template?
Which permission, secret or boundary does the change widen?
What does failure expose in logs, errors or defaults?

lenses.title: Simplicity
lenses.question: Is there less to build, depend on or maintain than this artifact proposes?
asks: Which part could be removed or replaced by an existing library or service?
Which new dependency, option or abstraction has one user?
What will a maintainer have to learn that the task did not require?

lenses.title: Operability
lenses.question: Can someone run, observe, diagnose and roll this back at 3 AM?
asks: Which failure leaves no log, metric or trace?
How is the change undone, and what state does rollback leave behind?
Which step needs a human who may not be there?

lenses.title: Migration and compatibility
lenses.question: What happens to existing clients, data and versions during and after the change?
asks: Which stored or serialized shape changes, and who reads the old shape?
What breaks when old and new versions run side by side?
Is there a safe order of rollout and a stated point of no return?

lenses.title: Cost and quota
lenses.question: What does this cost at expected and peak load, in money, tokens and rate limits?
asks: Which call, query or model invocation grows with input size or user count?
Which quota or rate limit is hit first?
Is the cost bounded by something other than good intentions?

lenses.title: Cold-read comprehension
lenses.question: Can a reader with no background follow it and act on it correctly?
asks: Which term, acronym or reference is used before it is defined?
Which step depends on knowledge only the author has?
Which sentence can be read two ways with different consequences?

lenses.title: Evidence and provenance
lenses.question: Is every claim tied to a source, a run or a named observation?
asks: Which claim has no citation, command output or file reference?
Which source was read in full, and which only skimmed or assumed?
What contrary evidence exists and was it reported?

lenses.title: Numbers and reconciliation
lenses.question: Do the figures add up, reconcile to their source and carry the right units?
asks: Which total does not equal the sum of its parts?
Which figure changes between two places in the artifact?
Which unit, period or rounding rule is unstated?

lenses.title: Authorization and final state
lenses.question: Was the action allowed, aimed at the right target, and is the end state the one requested?
asks: Who authorized each outward-facing or irreversible step, and where is that recorded?
Was the target the intended one, checked after the action?
Does the final observed state match the request, not just the last command's exit code?

lenses.title: Cross-artifact consistency
lenses.question: Do the artifacts agree with each other on names, numbers and references?
asks: Which name, ID or value differs between two artifacts?
Which reference points at something that moved or no longer exists?
Which statement in one artifact is contradicted by another?
